subject: Greenfield supplier portal: invite accepted but login fails (Coupa) — needs manual path
messages:
From: Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@greenfieldelec.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, it-support@greenfieldelec.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Can't accept supplier invite — Coupa shows 403 after clicking link

Hi Sergio,

We clicked the supplier invite you sent this morning and the Accept link goes to a Coupa page that returns a 403 (Forbidden). The invite looks OK in the email — we get the button and click it, then land on an error.

Steps we tried:
- Opened the invite in Chrome incognito (Win 10)
- Tried direct accept link copy/paste to new tab
- Tried from different machine behind our corporate proxy (same 403)

Error snippet (copied from the page):
403 — Access Denied
Request id: 0x1a4f2c3b4

I attached a screenshot of the error page and the raw invite EML. Our IT says it might be proxy header rewriting but wanted to loop you in. We need to onboard Greenfield as a vendor this week — PO is ready once they accept.

Attachments: login-screenshot-403.png, coupa-invite-email-raw.eml

Thanks,
Sara Nelson
Procurement Operations
Greenfield Electronics
[sara.nelson@greenfieldelec.com]

---
Forwarded-for context: we are a third-party supplier for Redwood's PO on ACME-291 (not needed by you, but FYI).
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@greenfieldelec.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — Coupa shows 403 after clicking link

Hi Sara — sorry you're hitting this. Thanks for the screenshot and EML, that helps. A few quick clarifying questions and a potential workaround so we don't block the PO: 

1) Can you confirm whether your org uses an outbound HTTP proxy that strips or rewrites Authorization / X-Forwarded-* headers? Our experience is that some proxies remove the relay-state or rewrite Host and break the Coupa accept flow.
2) If you have the proxy logs handy, please share the trace for the request to coupa.com (we only need a small window around the accept click).

Short-term workaround (two options):
- I can create the vendor record manually on your behalf in Coupa and provision a temp onboarding link that bypasses the SSO accept flow — you'll still need to confirm details but this gets the PO moving.
- Alternatively, if IT can whitelisted coupa-host and preserve the original Host/Referer headers for the accept path, that usually fixes it.

Ben — can you prepare the manual vendor creation checklist (I think we have a template) and confirm whether a temp "one-time" accept link is acceptable for Greenfield?
Laura — can you confirm whether this should be escalated to our Security team if proxy header rewriting is involved?

Sara — we'll try the manual path if you prefer. If you can attach the proxy trace and any corporate firewall notes, that will speed diagnostics.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

[Attachment placeholders referenced by Sara retained in thread]
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@greenfieldelec.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — Coupa shows 403 after clicking link

Sergio / Sara — I can own the manual vendor creation so Greenfield can receive the PO today. Attached is a quick checklist and the step-by-step I use when the portal flow fails.

Plan:
- Sara: if you agree, I'll create the vendor profile using the information in your EML and confirm the vendor email. I will not publish invoices; this is only to allow the PO to be issued and accepted.
- I'll mark the vendor record as "onboard pending validation" and add an onboarding note that IT should not revoke.

I also asked our infra team for a short troubleshooting checklist for the proxy behavior; if Sara can attach the small proxy trace (request headers, host, timestamp) that would let us confirm whether Header rewrite is the cause.

I've attached: manual_onboard_instructions.pdf (internal), and a one-page explanation for customers we can share.

Ben Carter
Manager, Customer Onboarding — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
[Attachment: manual_onboard_instructions.pdf]
From: Sara Nelson <sara.nelson@greenfieldelec.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, it-support@greenfieldelec.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Can't accept supplier invite — Coupa shows 403 after clicking link

Thanks — Ben and Sergio.

We attached the proxy trace as requested (proxy-trace-greenfield-20270316.txt) and the full raw EML for the invite (coupa-invite-email-raw.eml). IT confirmed their outbound gateway replaces the Host header for certain deep-link patterns for security inspection.

Excerpt from proxy trace (timestamp and headers):
---
2027-03-16T09:12:42Z GET https://supplier.coupa.com/accept?token=xxxxxxxx
Host: proxy.greenfield.local (original Host header replaced)
X-Forwarded-For: 10.8.3.4
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)
---

IT apologizes — they can whitelist the accept path but that will take until tomorrow morning (policy change + change window).

Given the PO timing, we prefer the manual vendor creation option now. Ben, please proceed with the manual profile and temporary link. Once Greenfield is set up we will follow up with IT to validate the real accept flow and revert if needed.

Thanks for the rapid responses. Please confirm when the temporary vendor record is created and share the record id so my finance team can attach the PO.

Best,
Sara Nelson
Procurement Operations
Greenfield Electronics
